prompt: Design a bounded work queue in Python for processing files with several worker threads. Explain ownership, backpressure, error propagation, cancellation, and shutdown. Include a concrete implementation sketch and tests for a worker failure and cancellation while the queue is full. Preserve input ordering in the returned results without serializing the workers. Explain what guarantees are possible when a worker is already inside a blocking file operation. Give enough detail to make the design directly implementable.

A factory has three machines. Machine A completes one part every 7 minutes, B every 11 minutes, and C every 13 minutes. They start simultaneously at time zero and complete their first parts after their respective processing times. Parts require no shared material or additional processing. Determine the earliest integer minute at which at least 100 parts have been completed. Show a rigorous method, compute the result, and verify that the immediately preceding minute is insufficient. Explain how to generalize the method to a million parts without simulating each minute.

Write an original scene about two librarians repairing a small coastal library after a storm. One wants to digitize every damaged book immediately; the other is concerned about provenance and the notes left in the margins. Develop their disagreement through dialogue and concrete physical details rather than a lecture. Let them agree on a practical first step without making either character completely right. Include a brief reflection on the distinction between preserving information and preserving an object.

Design a Rust service that reads records from a network connection, validates them, and writes batches to durable storage. Memory use must remain bounded when storage slows down. Explain the ownership and concurrency design, where backpressure is applied, how partial writes and retries are handled, and how shutdown avoids losing acknowledged records. Provide a small implementation outline and a focused testing strategy. Distinguish at-least-once delivery from exactly-once effects and identify the assumptions needed for the latter.

A reservoir starts with 750 liters. A pump adds 17 liters per minute during each of its first 8 minutes, then rests for 3 minutes, repeating this 11-minute cycle indefinitely. A separate drain removes 9 liters per minute continuously, including while the pump rests. Treat the changes as occurring at the end of each integer minute and assume unlimited reservoir capacity. Find the first minute at which the reservoir contains at least 1500 liters. Derive the answer using complete cycles and a remainder, then check the preceding minute explicitly.

Write an original scene in a mountain railway workshop on the evening before the line reopens. An experienced mechanic wants to preserve the old hand-written maintenance ledger, while a new engineer wants a searchable electronic record. Use dialogue and specific workshop details to explore the strengths and limits of both approaches. Give the characters a practical disagreement about one uncertain repair entry and let them design a process that records the uncertainty instead of concealing it. Avoid a simplistic victory for either character.
